I've been farming this same land since I was in my twenties. I know every patch of it. The soil here in Quzhou is decent — flat, good drainage when we get the summer rains, and my well has never let me down. Two of us at home now, kids are in the city. 7.8 mu is manageable for me alone, especially with the small tractor I rent from my neighbor.

**My thinking:**

The rotation is simple — wheat goes in October, harvest June, then straight into maize. Same 7.8 mu for both. I've done it this way for thirty years and it works.

For **wheat**, I'll use the Jimai variety seed I've been buying from the village supply station — it's improved seed, not the old stuff we saved ourselves. The yields are better. I put down base fertilizer before seeding — diammonium phosphate and urea — and then topdress with urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once at jointing stage in spring, once at heading, once at grain fill. I skip the winter water unless it's been very dry. Two pesticide sprays — herbicide in January or February when weeds start, and a fungicide at heading because rust hit us a few years back. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest in October before sowing. I expect around 450 jin per mu — call it 450 kg.

For **maize**, I always buy hybrid seed. Zhengdan 958 has done well for me. After wheat harvest I rotary-till the stubble, then plant right away — no time to waste in June. I apply urea twice, once at emergence and once at the big bell stage. Summer rains usually handle most of the water needs but I'll irrigate twice from the well if it's dry in July. One herbicide spray right after planting, one for corn borer mid-season. Expecting around 600 kg per mu.

At 61, I don't experiment much. I do what I know works. My two goals are: no crop failure, and not wearing myself out.
